a: A computer takes input, processes it with a CPU using instructions from memory (RAM), stores results on disk, and shows output on a screen. The CPU runs fetch-decode-execute cycles. Everything is binary (0/1). Software is layers of instructions that control the hardware.

Programming is writing precise instructions a computer can follow. You use a language (Python, C++, Lua, JS), describe data and steps, and the runtime or compiler turns that into actions. Good programs are clear, handle errors, and solve one problem well.

A language is the syntax and rules (JavaScript, Python). A framework is a ready structure built on a language that gives you patterns and tools (React on JS, Django on Python). Language = tools. Framework = a workshop layout that already has shelves and rules.

Devices talk over networks using IP addresses. DNS turns names (google.com) into IPs. TCP/UDP move packets. HTTP/HTTPS request pages. Routers forward packets hop by hop. Your browser asks a server; the server replies with HTML/JSON/files.

An API is a contract: how one program asks another for data or actions. REST APIs usually use HTTP methods (GET/POST) and JSON. You send a request to a URL, get a structured response. No need to know the other app's internal code.

A variable is a named box that holds a value. You create it, put data in, read it later, or change it. Types matter: numbers, strings, booleans, tables/objects. Scope decides where the name is visible.
A function is a named block of code you can call with inputs (parameters) and get an output (return). It avoids repeating the same steps. Good functions do one job and have clear names.

Loops repeat a block while a condition is true (while) or for a known range (for). for i=1,10 do ... end runs 10 times. while condition do ... end keeps going until the condition fails. Infinite loops freeze your program — always have an exit.

RAM is fast temporary storage the CPU uses while running. Disk is slower permanent storage. When a program runs, code and data load into RAM. When it exits, RAM is freed. Memory leaks happen when you keep allocating without freeing.

Client is the program the user runs (browser, game, app). Server is the program that waits for requests and answers them (website backend, game server). Client asks, server responds. They talk over the network.

Debugging is finding why code does the wrong thing. Read the error, check values with prints or a debugger, shrink the problem to the smallest case that fails, fix that, re-test. Guess less, observe more.

Encryption scrambles data with a key so only someone with the right key can read it. Symmetric = same key both ways (AES). Asymmetric = public key to lock, private key to unlock (RSA). HTTPS uses both.
Open source means the source code is public. Anyone can read, use, modify, and often share changes under a license. You still own your project; the license sets the rules.
Frontend is what the user sees and clicks (HTML/CSS/JS, UI). Backend is the server logic, database, auth, APIs. Frontend talks to backend over HTTP. Full-stack means both.

A database stores structured data so you can query it fast. SQL databases use tables and queries (SELECT, INSERT). NoSQL stores documents or key-value pairs. Apps save user data, posts, scores there instead of files alone.

Roblox runs Luau scripts on the client and server. Client scripts handle local UI and input. Server scripts own the real game state. RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions bridge them. Exploiters inject client scripts; server authority is the real defense.

An external reads/writes the game process from outside (another process). It usually uses ReadProcessMemory/WriteProcessMemory or a driver, draws an overlay (ImGui + DirectX), and does world-to-screen for ESP/aim. It does not inject code into the game unless designed to.

Aimbot finds enemy positions in memory or via engine, converts 3D world coords to 2D screen (W2S), picks a target by FOV/distance/priority, then moves the camera or mouse toward that point. Silent aim writes angles without moving the visible crosshair the same way.
World-to-screen (W2S) multiplies a 3D position by the view-projection matrix and divides by w to get 2D screen coordinates. Used for ESP boxes, tracers, and aim. Bad matrix = wrong boxes.
Create a transparent topmost window, init DirectX/OpenGL, run ImGui each frame, draw menus and ESP on top of the game. Color-key or layered window styles keep the game visible underneath.

Python is strong for scripts, data, and backend; syntax is clean, one way to do many things. JavaScript runs in every browser and on Node; async-first, flexible, messy if you let it. Python = clarity. JS = everywhere on the web.

C++ is compiled, fast, manual memory, used for engines and externals. Lua/Luau is interpreted, tiny, embeddable, used inside games (Roblox). C++ for performance and system control. Lua for fast game logic and scripting.

Stack holds local variables and call frames; automatic and fast, limited size. Heap is for dynamic allocations (new/malloc); you manage lifetime, can grow large, slower. Stack overflow vs memory leak.

q: what is a process vs thread
a: A process is a running program with its own memory. Threads are workers inside one process that share memory. Multiple threads can do work in parallel but need locks when they touch the same data.
GET reads. POST creates/sends body. PUT replaces. PATCH updates part. DELETE removes. Status codes: 200 ok, 400 bad request, 401 auth, 404 missing, 500 server error.
JSON is a text format for data: objects {"key":"value"}, arrays [1,2], strings, numbers, true/false/null. Easy for humans and machines. APIs and configs use it everywhere.

Pick one language. Build tiny projects that interest you. Read errors. Change one thing at a time. Copy working code then rewrite it yourself. Consistency beats intensity. Ship something ugly before perfect.

Git tracks versions of your files. commit saves a snapshot. branch experiments without breaking main. push/pull sync with a remote (GitHub). You can undo mistakes and collaborate without overwriting each other.
Variables can change after you set them. Constants stay the same once set. Use constants for values that should never flip (PI, max players). Makes bugs rarer and intent clearer.
A function that calls itself with a smaller problem until a base case stops it. Good for trees and divide-and-conquer. Bad if the base case is missing — stack overflow.

q: how does a browser render a page
a: Parse HTML into a DOM tree, CSS into styles, combine into a render tree, layout positions and sizes, paint pixels. JS can change the DOM and trigger re-layout. Heavy JS or huge DOM = lag.
Latency is delay (how long one bit takes to arrive). Bandwidth is throughput (how many bits per second). Low latency matters for games and aim. High bandwidth matters for downloads.
Authentication = who are you (login, token, HWID). Authorization = what are you allowed to do (admin, read-only). You can be logged in but still denied an action.
When two threads or clients touch the same data at the same time and the result depends on order. Fix with locks, atomic ops, or single-threaded ownership. Common in multiplayer and UI code.
The runtime finds objects no longer reachable from roots and frees them. You don't free by hand (JS, Luau, Python). Cost is pauses and less control. C++ has no GC by default — you own deletes.

REST is request-response over HTTP; simple, cacheable, one answer per ask. WebSocket is a persistent two-way channel; good for live chat, game state, streaming. Use REST for APIs, WS for continuous updates.

q: what is an offset in cheats
a: An offset is the distance from a module base or object pointer to a field (health, position, team). Game updates move them. Dumpers and pattern scans find new ones. Hardcoding old offsets breaks after patches.

Force another process to load your DLL so your code runs inside it. Common methods: LoadLibrary via CreateRemoteThread, manual map (write sections yourself, no LoadLibrary). Used for hooks and internals.

q: what is a driver in cheats
a: A kernel driver runs at ring-0 and can read/write any process memory and hide better from usermode AC. Higher power, higher ban/risk surface, needs signing or vulnerable driver abuse (BYOVD).
Measure first. Hot loops and allocations matter. Cache results. Avoid work off-screen. Batch draws. Profile before rewriting. Premature optimization wastes time; late optimization saves the product.
A pointer holds a memory address. *p reads the value there. &x is the address of x. Null pointers crash. Dangling pointers point at freed memory. Core of C/C++ and cheat memory work.
Binary is base-2 (bits). Hex is base-16, compact way to write bytes (0xFF = 255). Memory dumps, offsets, and colors often use hex. One byte = two hex digits.

q: what is an event in programming
a: An event is a signal that something happened (click, player joined, message received). You register a handler/callback that runs when the event fires. Decouples producer from consumer.
Index documents offline (words → which docs contain them). At query time, look up terms, rank by relevance (TF-IDF, BM25, embeddings). Return top hits. Same idea as keyword scoring in this AI.

q: what is training data for ai
a: Examples the model learns from: question→answer pairs, text, code, labels. Quality and coverage beat raw size. This backend learns by adding scored Q/A samples you train, not by gradient descent.
Compare = show similarities and differences. Contrast = focus on differences. Good answers name both sides, give a concrete example, then a one-line takeaway.
A system that is always in one named state and only moves on defined transitions. Menus, game modes, connection status. Clear states beat boolean soup.
Store expensive results and reuse them until they go stale. Browser cache, CDN, in-memory maps. Wrong cache = stale bugs. Right cache = speed.
Doing the same operation multiple times leaves the same result as doing it once. GET and PUT are usually idempotent. POST often is not. Useful for safe retries.

q: explain why code breaks after updates
a: APIs change, offsets move, assumptions die. Pin versions, detect layout changes, fail closed, keep a derivation path for new addresses. Games and OS patches are why cheat offsets and signatures expire.

q: what is a race in multiplayer
a: Two clients claim the same resource at once (item pickup, door). Server must decide the winner. Trust the server, not the client.

q: how to write a good answer
a: Lead with the direct answer. Add one short why. Give a concrete example. End with a practical next step. Skip filler. Match the asker's depth.
Compiled languages turn source into machine code ahead of time (C++). Interpreted run source (or bytecode) at runtime (Python, Luau). Compiled = faster execution. Interpreted = faster iteration.

q: what is a library vs package
a: Library = reusable code you link or import. Package = library plus metadata and install story (npm, pip, NuGet). Same idea at different packaging levels.
Never trust user or network input. Check type, length, range, format. Reject early. Prevents crashes, injections, and bad state. Fail closed.
Two threads each wait for a lock the other holds. Nothing moves. Avoid by consistent lock order, timeouts, or fewer locks.
You type a name. Resolver asks root → TLD → authoritative servers for the IP. Caches speed repeats. Wrong DNS = site unreachable even if the server is up.
Code that sits between request and handler: logging, auth, CORS, rate limits. Same pattern in Express, ASP.NET, game tick pipelines.
Test one small piece in isolation with known input and expected output. Fast feedback. Catches regressions when you change code later.
Automatically build and test every push so broken main is rare. CI is a safety net, not a substitute for thinking.
Local = full control, no sleep, your hardware. Cloud free tiers sleep and limit CPU. Paid cloud scales and stays up. This AI uses free Render — first hit can be slow after idle.
When a free host spins a sleeping service back up. First request waits 30–60s. Keep-alive pings or paid always-on fix it.
No neural net. Tokenize the question, score each training sample by shared words and tags, return the best match above a threshold. Train by adding better Q→A pairs. Simple, free, controllable.
The text you send the AI. Clear prompts with keywords match training samples better. Vague prompts get weak scores.
Admin opens Train AI, types question and answer, optional tag, saves with pin. Sample is appended to learned_samples.json and used on next chats. More good pairs = smarter replies.
Hardware ID — a fingerprint from disk, board, CPU, etc. License systems lock a key to one machine. Reset policies vary (e.g. month keys get one reset).
Day = short trial window, lowest price. Week = balance. Month = longest, sometimes one HWID reset. Same verify API, different expiry.
A transparent topmost window drawn over the game. Used for menus and ESP without injecting into the game process (external style).
Field of view circle around crosshair. Only targets inside the FOV are considered. Smaller FOV = more legit look, fewer targets.
Aim that adjusts shot angles or hit registration without visibly yanking the camera the same way. Different detection surface than hard lock.
When crosshair is on a valid target (color, entity, or ray), simulate or send the fire input. Often combined with aim assist.
Extra sensory perception in cheats: boxes, names, health, skeletons drawn on enemies through walls using W2S positions.
Cull distant entities, limit ESP draw count, lower update rate off-combat, avoid per-frame heavy scans, use dirty flags. Less work per frame = higher FPS.
4x4 matrix from the camera that transforms world coordinates into clip space. Required for correct W2S. Read from the game each frame or on camera change.

q: how to structure a cheat ui
a: Tabs by job (Combat, Visuals, Movement, Misc, Settings). Toggle + slider per feature. Save/load configs. Keybinds. Status line for attach/FPS.
Load a DLL by writing its sections into the target yourself and fixing relocations/imports, without calling LoadLibrary. Harder to see in module lists.
Host and injected DLL map the same named section. Write commands and results there, signal with events. Faster and often cleaner than named pipes for local IPC.
Unified naming convention — a catalog of functions executors expose (print, game, http, filesystem, crypt, etc.) so scripts run across executors with fewer ifs.

q: how identity works in luau executors
a: identifyexecutor / getexecutorname return the product name. Scripts branch on that. Spoofing is possible but server should not trust client identity.
First Luau chunk the executor runs to set up environment, hooks, and UNC stubs before user scripts.
Internal runs inside the game process (hooks, full engine access, higher detection risk). External runs outside (RPM/WPM, overlay, usually safer from some ACs, limited to what memory exposes).
Search memory for a unique byte pattern to find a function or global when offsets move. Masks allow wildcards. Core of version-resilient cheats.
PE (Windows EXE/DLL) has headers and sections (.text code, .data, .rdata, etc.). Manual mappers copy and protect them correctly or the process dies.
Direct request to the kernel (Nt* / Zw*). Going through ntdll can be hooked by EDR; indirect/direct syscalls skip some usermode hooks.
OpenProcess with rights, ReadProcessMemory (or driver). Need correct address and size. Handle ASLR by resolving module base + offset each run.
Address space layout randomization — module bases change each launch. Always resolve base at runtime; never hardcode absolute addresses.
Each frame: NewFrame, build widgets, Render, present. State lives across frames. Don't recreate fonts every frame.
Sync present to monitor refresh. Stops tearing, can add latency. Off for lowest input lag in competitive overlays.
Serialize toggles/sliders to JSON or binary, write to disk, load on start. Version the format so old configs don't crash new builds.
Map virtual-key codes to actions. Support toggle vs hold. Ignore binds while typing in ImGui text fields.
Snapshot entity list each tick or on interval: pointer, team, health, position. Aim/ESP read the cache, not raw memory every pixel.
Skip allies so you don't aim or highlight teammates. Read team id or name from memory / engine.
Skip entities farther than max distance for ESP/aim. Saves CPU and reduces clutter.
Ray or engine trace from camera to target; only aim/ESP if not blocked. More legit, more work, more engine dependency.
Instead of snapping, interpolate current angles toward target over time. Smoothing factor controls legit look vs speed.
Target a skeleton bone (head, chest) instead of origin. Requires bone matrix read. More precise.
Detect version, re-dump offsets, update signatures, keep a changelog. Automate what you can; never assume last week's addresses.
Write timed messages to console or file. Levels: error, warn, info, debug. First tool when something fails only on his machine.
If a check fails or data is missing, disable the feature instead of guessing. Safer than acting on bad pointers.

q: what is a design doc for cheats
a: List features, memory sources, UI tabs, config keys, attach flow, and failure modes before coding. Stops feature soup mid-build.

q: compare mouse move and angle write
a: Mouse move sends input to the OS/game. Angle write patches camera/view angles in memory. Different detection and feel.
Named offset into an entity class in Source-like engines. Dumped from recv tables. Similar idea exists in other engines under different names.
Filter valid enemies, score by FOV, distance, health, threat. Pick best score. Sticky aim holds last target until invalid.
Hotkey that toggles overlay visibility. Common: Insert, RShift, Home. Don't conflict with game binds.
ImGui often uses ImVec4 0–1 floats. GDI uses 0–255. Hex #RRGGBB. Convert carefully or colors look washed or neon.
On high-DPI screens, coordinates scale. Mark the overlay DPI-aware or W2S and clicks misalign.

q: how multi monitor works for overlay
a: Track the game window rect, move/resize overlay to match. Fullscreen exclusive is harder than borderless.
Snapshot of process state at crash. Analyze in WinDbg/VS to see the faulting address and stack. Essential for heisenbugs.
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Breaking change = major. Feature = minor. Fix = patch. Helps users and loaders know compatibility.
Small program that fetches the real binary or script, checks license, then injects or executes. Keeps the payload updatable.
Client sends key + HWID to /v1/verify. Server checks expiry, HWID lock, status. Returns ok or reason. Offline grace is optional.
Cap requests per time window to stop abuse. Return 429 when exceeded. Protects free backends from spam.
Browser rule: pages can only call certain other origins unless the server sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin. This API allows * for the static site.
Starter training samples shipped with the AI so it is not empty on day one. You grow it with Train AI.

q: how to make answers less dumb
a: More targeted samples, better scoring (penalize weak overlap), mode detection (code vs emotion vs compare), dictionary for unknown words, and a think step that restates the ask before answering.
Combine related words or definitions into one richer reply — synonyms, antonyms, example sentence — so the AI does not answer with a single bare term.
When the user asks to search or look up, prefer dictionary/API lookup and keyword scan over random chat samples. Return structured hits.
Before the final answer, briefly name the intent (compare, define, code, emotion) and the key terms. Improves match quality and transparency.
If the prompt is Spanish or mixed, look up words via RAE-style or free dictionary APIs and merge definitions into the reply. Same for English unknown words.
No paid LLM API. Node on Render free tier, JSON samples on disk, keyword scoring in process. Cost is your time training it.
